title: WRITE(*, ...) and WRITE(6, ...) — implicit-default vs hardcoded unit 6 may diverge under redirection
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE TRACE(MSG)
C     WRITE(*, ...) is 'the default output unit' (compiler picks --
C     usually stdout). WRITE(6, ...) is hardcoded unit 6 (which on
C     traditional Unix Fortran maps to stdout, but on IBM mainframe
C     systems is a JCL SYSOUT slot). A direct port that maps both
C     to System.out works on the Unix flavour but loses the JCL
C     redirection on the IBM flavour.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      CHARACTER*(*) MSG
      WRITE (*, '(A)') MSG
      END
notes: Trace/log output via WRITE(*, ) or WRITE(6, ) is everywhere. The Java/C# port usually goes through a logger interface; the spec must surface this so the rewrite uses an abstraction (SLF4J / ILogger) and not hardcoded System.out.
